title: Cross-functional SLAs and Capacity Delegation Guide
author: Asha Verma
content:
Summary:
This guide defines a cross-functional approach to SLAs, SLOs, error budgets, and capacity delegation between SRE, product/owner teams, and tenant/platform teams. The goal is predictable reliability while giving product teams responsibility for feature-level availability and SRE responsibility for fleet-level capacity and safe-guards.

Scope:
- Applies to all customer-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments) operated by Redwood.
- Includes multi-tenant services (model serving, embedding pipelines, batch/streaming inference) and their associated supporting infra (gateway, routing, cache).

Definitions and principles:
- SLA: A contractual commitment (external). Handled by Sales/Legal with SRE input.
- SLO: A measurable service objective used internally to guide operations (e.g., 99.9% successful-gen within latency target).
- Error budget: The allowed rate of SLO violations over a rolling period (commonly 30d).
- Delegated capacity: Reserved capacity quota entrusted to a product/tenant team for guaranteed throughput.
- Capacity escrow: A short-term set-aside of physical capacity for rapid use during incidents or launches.

Key design principles:
- Clear ownership: SRE owns platform capacity envelope; product teams own feature-level SLOs and alerts.
- Transparent economics: Per-tenant cost impact of delegated capacity must be visible in console.
- Fail-open vs fail-safe: Default is fail-open for non-critical features (best-effort); critical features must declare fail-safe fallbacks.
- Single source of truth: SLO definitions, runbooks, and capacity reservations live in the Redwood Console and this repo of playbooks.

Ownership matrix (high level):
| Concern | Primary owner | Secondary owner | Decision authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fleet capacity provisioning | SRE | Eng Infra | SRE (with Product consult) |
| Model selection/rollout | Product/ML | SRE | Product/ML |
| Feature SLO definitions | Product/Owner team | SRE | Product/Owner team |
| Emergency capacity release | SRE | Product | SRE (operational) |
| Error budget arbitration | SRE & Product | Customer Success | Cross-functional committee |

SLO and error-budget governance
1) SLO template (required fields):
- service_name (string)
- objective (e.g., 99.9%)
- metric (e.g., successful_generation / total_requests)
- latency_bound (ms) or qualitative outcome (e.g., correctness threshold)
- evaluation_window (30d default)
- alert_thresholds (burn_rate > 2x for 1h, 4x for 30m)
- owner (email/alias)

2) Example SLO (text):
- Service: hosted-text-generation
- Objective: 99.9% of requests return a completion within 300ms p50 and 1.5s p95, and successful token stream without error
- Error budget: 0.1% daily allowance, evaluated on rolling 30d window

3) Error budget banking and cross-tenant pooling:
- Per-tenant error budgets are primary. Teams may opt into a limited pooled budget for burst events (max retention 7 days) to facilitate controlled launches.
- Banking rules: unused daily error budget can be banked up to 3x daily allowance; banking beyond that requires SRE approval.
- Pooling rules: a tenant can request temporary access to pool; SRE will authorize if pool health (available capacity headroom > 15% and fleet burn_rate < 0.8).

Capacity delegation protocol
Phase A — Request and justification:
1. Product/tenant files a capacity-delegation request via the Console form including expected QPS, percent of/p95 tail, time window, and expected duration. Attach load-test artifacts.
2. SRE reviews request within 48 business hours, verifying load profile against historical telemetry.

Phase B — Approval and configuration:
1. SRE may approve one of: a) Dedicated quota (hard limit), b) Burst escrow (temporal cushion), c) Managed shared quota (soft limit with throttling policies).
2. Configuration includes: reserved GPU count, routing policy ID, admission controller tags, and cost center assignment. SRE provides IaC fragment to commit to tenant config.

Phase C — Operational handoff:
1. SRE publishes a delegated capacity dashboard (latency, queue-depth, token-rate, error-rate) scoped to the tenant.
2. Product owners are added to the capacity-alerting rotation and must maintain runbook readiness.

Operational tooling integrations
- Telemetry hooks required for delegation: request_id propagation, tenant_id tag, model_variant, routing_path, queuing_time_ms, GPU_util_pct, kv_cache_hit_rate.
- Console views: per-tenant headroom, projected burn-rate, cost-per-1000-tokens, active-reservations.
- Automation: Accepts CLI commands for emergency-release and escrow-expansion with RBAC (examples below).

Runbook excerpts (emergency capacity bind)
1) Trigger: product reports sustained p95 latency > target for 10m and queue-depth increase > 2x baseline.
2) Triage steps (chronological):
   a) Confirm telemetry: open tenant dashboard, confirm latency and GPU_util_pct.
   b) Check model variants: is there an older quantized variant available for fallback? If yes, set routing policy to fallback (see routing-policy CLI sample).
   c) If fallback insufficient, SRE evaluates emergency escrow release:
      - Verify pool health: overall fleet error_rate < 1% and available physical headroom >= requested GPUs.
      - Run preflight scaling canary (deploy 1 pod to a target host and validate latency with synthetic tracer).
   d) Execute emergency-release CLI (RBAC) with annotation linking to incident ID.
   e) Communicate to product and CS: update incident ticket with release time and expected impact.

3) Post-incident reconciliation:
- SRE and Product complete an incident-initiation form in Retroboard within 48h.
- Any escrow usage beyond 8 hours triggers chargeback or repatriation plan (see Cost and chargeback table).

Incident review and evidence standards
- Evidence required for incident review:
  * telemetry snapshot (30m pre/post),
  * request traces (sampled set, min 100 requests),
  * model input corpus snippet (redaction required),
  * configuration changes (IaC commits) and rollout timeline,
  * error budget burn reports.
- Postmortem checklist (deliverables within 72h):
  1) Annotated timeline (ISO timestamps)
  2) Root cause hypothesis and verification steps
  3) List of corrective actions with owners and ETA
  4) SLO recalibration proposal (if applicable)

Decision and arbitration process
- Minor disputes (e.g., short-term escrow denials) resolved by SRE lead + product manager.
- Material disputes (affecting contracts or multi-tenant guarantees) escalate to Reliability Council (SRE director, Head of Product, Head of CS, Finance rep).
- Arbitration signals include: >3 tenants requesting emergency escrow within 24h, sustained fleet burn_rate > 1.5 for 4h, or cross-region failure correlation.

Cost and chargeback (summary table)
| Item | Trigger | Billing rule |
|---|---:|---|
| Escrow use (short) | < 8h | No immediate charge; internal AR ticket created |
| Escrow use (long) | >= 8h | Automated charge by cost-center; prorated GPU-hours at committed rate |
| Dedicated delegated quota | Reservation commit | Monthly invoice based on reserved GPU-hours |

CLI / IaC examples (samples)
- Emergency release (RBAC required):
  redwoodctl capacity release --tenant tenant-42 --gpus 4 --reason "p95-latency-surge" --incident-id INC-2026-1543

- Example reservation fragment (YAML):
  reservation:
    tenant_id: tenant-42
    reserved_gpus: 8
    routing_policy: "policy-ml-fastpath-v2"
    escrow_expiry: "2026-03-01T08:00:00Z"

Observability and analytics requirements
- SRE will maintain a "capacity forecast" job that projects required headroom for the next 14d with daily cadence. Inputs: historical QPS, trending growth, scheduled launches, and pooled banking levels.
- Alerts must include: burn_rate(1h) > 2x, headroom < 10% for two consecutive evaluation windows, and sustained queue_depth_growth > 50% for 30m.

Templates and attachments (stored in Console):
- Delegation request form template (JSON schema)
- Incident evidence submission checklist (CSV)
- IaC sample repo link: git://git.redwood/services/capacity-delegation/examples

Appendix A — Quick decision matrix (condensed)
- Is the request predictable? -> Yes -> request Dedicated quota; No -> request Burst escrow + managed throttling.
- Is the pool healthy? -> No -> SRE denies escrow and offers staged canary.

Appendix B — Example SLO JSON (copy into console):
{
  "service_name": "hosted-text-generation",
  "objective": "99.9%",
  "metric": "successful_responses / total_requests",
  "latency_p95_ms": "1500",
  "evaluation_window": "30d",
  "owner": "team-hosted-ml@redwood.com"
}

Contact & escalation paths:
- Primary SRE oncall alias: sre-oncall@redwood.com
- Capacity governance mailbox: capacity-gov@redwood.com
- Reliability Council chair: lina@redwood.com
